why: Django's ticket tracker forbids automated use of its own search (robots.txt: Disallow /search and /query). A web search engine's index of the tracker was searched instead, and each ticket it returned that bears on the subject was fetched by number, which robots.txt allows. An index does not hold every ticket, so this is not a full search of the tracker.

searches.tool: web search limited to the domain code.djangoproject.com

results.title: Minimize the risk of SECRET_KEY leaks
results.read: fetched and read, maintainers-trac-20081.html; 2013 to 2020. In the description the reporter, shown as Jacob, asks of a proposal to generate the key on start-up: "How does this handle multiple web servers, though? Seems like if you weren't careful you'd end up with differing secrets across your web nodes, bad news." The other speaker, shown as Paul, answers: "Yeah, the multiple servers deployment its downside". Comment 9 (2014-02-23), by a contributor: "if someone moves from N=1 to N>1 deployment, they will silently start using different secret keys ... users will encounter random failures with some features". Comment 10 (2014-05-23), by a commenter: "the key must remain the same in multi-server environments".
